event: The night the curtain stayed down. Two minutes before the opening, the performance was stopped and the audience was sent home.

lenses.name: Ilse, who was playing the lead
Bram, the stagehand on the last check

objects.name: the prompt book, open at the first page
the ticket ledger for that night

lines.actor.prompt: Ilse reads the pencil note, 'HOLD — Bram, 7:58', and frowns: 'I was in my first costume. Nobody told us why.'
lines.actor.ledger: Ilse runs a finger down the refunds: 'Three hundred and twelve people came to see us, and we sent them home.'
lines.actor.rigging: Ilse reads 'second fly line frayed' and goes quiet. 'That line holds the bridge I stand on in act two.'
lines.box.prompt: The clerk notes the time, 7:58: 'Two minutes before curtain. Far too late to sell those seats to anyone else.'
lines.box.ledger: The clerk adds it up: 312 refunds, the biggest loss of the season, and two school groups that will not book again.
lines.box.rigging: The clerk reads the repair cost beside the refund total: 'A new rope costs less than one row of seats.'
lines.stage.prompt: It is Bram's own note. 'HOLD. I called it. I would call it again.'
lines.stage.ledger: Bram shrugs at the ledger. 'Refunds can be paid back next week. A fall cannot be paid back.'
lines.stage.rigging: Bram's log, in a quick hand: 'Second fly line frayed at the cleat. Found at 7:55 on the last check. Show held.'

missing.stage: Edda taps the table. 'Your account never says why the show stopped. Bram is sitting in the wings, and nobody asked him.'
missing.rigging: Hari looks at the cards. 'Nobody in your account has looked at the rope. We are arguing about a reason we have not seen.'
missing.ledger: Hari turns over a card. 'Nobody counted what it cost. Three hundred people went home, and the house has to answer for that too.'
missing.actor: Edda says quietly, 'And the company? Nobody asked the people who were dressed and waiting.'

titles.reply: Edda nods. 'True. And to Ilse that night, it felt like being left in the dark. A title that is true can still leave someone out.'

titles.text: The most costly night of the season
titles.reply: Hari sighs. 'Also true. But a reader who sees only that title will ask who to blame, and the answer will be wrong.'

titles.text: A night the house chose a rope over three hundred seats
titles.reply: Edda and Hari read it twice. 'It names the choice,' says Hari. 'And it lets a reader argue with it,' says Edda.
